5 scientists + 11 AI wingmen in one live Scion Grove—not isolated chat tabs.

Building production-ready agentic science that a pharma portfolio review committee can sign off on requires addressing four core challenges:

Figure 2 — The 4 challenges in production pharmaceutical R&D: Rigid Workflows, Chatbot Fabrication, Single-Model Echo Chambers, and Lack of Organizational Governance. 🔍 Click to enlarge
Discovery ChallengeWhat Breaks in Standard Pipelines / ChatbotsHow GCP-OASE Solves It
1. The Rigid Workflow Problem Static pipelines (Nextflow, Snakemake) drop a target when bulk RNA-seq returns near-zero expression and cannot pause for multi-week wet-lab assays. Dynamic routing & lab handoff gates: Pivots to single-cell data when bulk tissue is low, and pauses on disk across multi-week wet-lab CRO assays.
2. The Chatbot Fabrication Trap Summarizes large tables in prompt context, invents plausible binding numbers, pads citations, or confuses NA with 0. Two-phase execution & dual validation: Deterministic Phase-1/2 tools write raw SHA-256 receipts and check human-defined cutoffs offline before AI Program Lead peer review.
3. The Single-Model Echo Chamber Uses a single model family to generate hypotheses, interpret literature, and review its own work, reinforcing correlated bias. Multi-model agent teams: Runs Gemini, Claude, and OpenAI side-by-side inside a shared Grove for blind hypothesis tournaments and cross-model review.
4. Lack of Organizational Governance in Foundation Models General-purpose LLMs lack a pharma organization's stage-gate criteria, risk tolerance, and decision-making rigor. Clear separation of powers across 5 artifact layers: Raw data files, specialist findings, scientific decision logs, organization stage gates, and executive views.

Act I (Part 2) — GCP-OASE Data and Control Architecture

1. The Grove · 2. Work Orders & Dual Validation · 3. Two-Phase Tool Execution · 4. Stage-Gate Review
Figure 4 — Four core solutions: Dynamic Routing & Lab Gates, Two-Phase Tool Execution & Dual Validation, Multi-Model Agent Teams, and 5-Layer Separation of Powers. 🔍 Click to enlarge
Figure 5 — The 4 Core Pillars: 1. The Grove, 2. Work Orders & Dual Validation, 3. Two-Phase Tool Execution, and 4. Stage-Gate Review. 🔍 Click to enlarge

1. The Grove ("Who is doing the work?")

Shared project workspace on SCION where the 5-scientist human pod and mirrored AI agent team (Gemini, Claude, OpenAI) collaborate. Specialists write findings to their own folders; only the AI Program Lead writes official decisions.

2. Work Orders & Dual Validation ("How is work checked?")

Every assignment is a numbered Work Order (WO-001..WO-008). Before closure, every finding must pass automated data-integrity verification (oase validate check) plus an independent scientific peer review by the AI Program Lead.

3. Two-Phase Tool Execution ("Why trust the numbers?")

Phase 1 (Data Acquisition) processes primary datasets with deterministic tools and saves raw outputs + SHA-256 provenance records (.meta.json). Phase 2 (Threshold Evaluation) evaluates outputs offline against human expert-defined program cutoffs (.analysis.json) and attaches required caveats.

4. Stage-Gate Review ("Who decides to move forward?")

Work orders roll up into five logged gates: 1. Target validation (AI + human sign), 2. Hit ID (AI signs, logs liabilities), 3. Lead opt (AI signs once resolved), 4. Lab handoff (human signs; pauses on disk), and 5. Candidate nomination (AI + human sign).

2.5-Hour (150-Minute) Guided Workshop & Hands-On Lab Playbook (`pcsk9-oral`)

0:00–2:30 · 3 "What Ifs" · 5 Scientist Seats · 6 Hands-On Blocks

Part 0 (`0:00–0:15` · 15 min) — Open With Three "What If" Provocations, Then Pivot: "Well — We Built It."

Before opening a terminal or architecture diagram, put these three questions to the discovery scientists and platform leads in the room and debate where today's chatbots and static DAGs break:

Slide / Question 1 · Multiplayer Grove
"What if we had an agentic AI surface all of our scientists could use together at the same time?"

Demonstrate 2+ human scientists typing simultaneously inside one shared Scion Grove alongside 11 specialist AI agents.

Slide / Question 2 · Zero Vendor Lock-In
"What if we had optionality in the frontier models we use—not locking our science into one vendor or one model's blind spots?"

Show Gemini, Anthropic Claude, and OpenAI collaborating via portable tiers so no model family ever reviews its own work.

Slide / Question 3 · Verified Governance
"What if every AI-assisted claim, threshold check, and stage-gate decision was cryptographically verified against raw data?"

Let participants actively tamper with raw files and findings in Block 4—and watch oase validate check block every violation in <1s.

Assign the 5 Discovery Pod Seats (Individual or 2–4 Person Breakout Pods)

Each chapter video is 36–43 seconds long to establish crisp context; spend the remaining 15–25 minutes of each block in live Scion Webchat Q&A, CLI inspection, and scientific debate across the 5 roles:
